messages:
maria: Heads up — a few customers reported their streaming clients hang after the connection says "reconnecting..." but never resumes. Seen on canary in us-west-2 after yesterday's routing policy change.

alex: saw same briefly. Logs show 499 (client closed) then server throws 'resume token unknown'. suspect route-switch invalidates resume id mapping.

sam: metrics: stream_resume_failures spiked x20 for the canary tenants. QoS buckets show higher p95 latency for resume ops.

infra-bot: deploy @alex rolled out routing/route-affinity v2 to canary (168 hosts) at 2024-08-03T11:02Z 

alex: reproducer: curl to streaming endpoint, then trigger route swap by changing policy on tenant. Server responds 200 then SSE stops. resume header we send is `Resume-Id: r_abc123`. New route expects `resume-id: R-abc123` (case/format normalization bug).

alex: ```bash
# client request
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Resume-Id: r_abc123
Accept: text/event-stream

# after route flip server side lookup expects
Resume-Id: R-abc123
```

jina: ah that's on us — we changed canonicalization in route-affinity rollout to uppercase the first char when generating resume ids. Fix: accept case-insensitive resume ids and normalize internally. Also add telemetry tag `route_id` on resume_fail.

maria: can we patch heuristics quickly? fallback to full reconnect after N ms so clients don't hang.

alex: I'll push a canary fix to accept case-insensitive tokens + add metric `resume_id_normalized` + console alert.

sam: please also add a console graph for resume_failures by tenant and a table correlating `route_change_event` with `resume_fail`. makes debugging faster for support.

maria: I'll pause the rest of the rollout until canary stabilizes. thanks all :thumbsup:
